what: Criterion 6: the command the owner runs to see slice 5's returning-raider detour, verified on this working copy before being put in the PR body — not assembled from memory or from documentation.
background: docs/design/SLICE_05_RETURNING_HERO.md §6.3 documents the detour as observable on baseline/20260729, naming two raiders: Крюк Немой (escaped wave 1, heavy scar, remembers (24,7)) and Секира (escaped wave 2, light scar, remembers (23,7)). scripts/run-game.ps1 had no -Seed before this Issue, so the owner's ordinary launch (baseline's own seed, 20260726) never reaches this: on 20260726 the only survivor with a scar remembers (14,7), the larder tile itself, which the design contract's §6.2 explicitly excludes from avoidance (a memory never takes away the objective) — so nothing to see. -Seed is what makes 20260729 reachable through the sanctioned entry point.

interactiveCommand.whatYouSeeThatsNew: The same graybox window as any other run-game.ps1 launch, but the party plays out on seed 20260729 instead of the fixture's own 20260726 — the seed the slice-5 design doc's detour evidence (evidence/358-memory.json) was captured on.
interactiveCommand.whatToWatch: Paused at tick 1 by design (an interactive launch always starts there — Main.cs forces LoadFixture's tick target to 1 whenever no -ScreenshotPath is given). Press [4] for 16x speed, then [P] to run. Wave 3 starts at tick 2000 and ends by tick 2055 (dotnet test evidence below). Watch for a raider carrying a two-line name tag — 'Крюк Немой' / 'волна 1 · едва не добили (24,7)' — entering from the gate at the top-right and walking toward the kitchen/larder along the row-7 corridor. He never steps on tile (24,7): the corridor has a parallel row (row 8) directly below it, and he takes the one-tile detour around the blocked cell instead. A second raider, 'Секира' (wave 2, light scar, remembers (23,7)), does the same in wave 4 (tick 2350-2401).

verifiedScreenshotCommand.why: A static frame cannot show a route, but it can show the one fact a picture is uniquely suited to prove: the label is actually rendered, on the actual raider, during an actual party — not just claimed by a document. This is the command actually run on this working copy, not written from memory.

verifiedScreenshotCommand.whatTheImageShows: Wave 3 in progress, five raiders visible near the kitchen/larder area. One of them carries the two-line name tag 'Крюк Немой' with a second line naming his wave and the tile he was hit on — ReturningHeroLabel (docs/design/SLICE_05_RETURNING_HERO.md §8), drawn only over a raider with a scar and a remembered place (§8.2). This is the sanctioned-entry-point proof that slice 5's naming mechanism is live on the seed the design doc's detour claim was measured on; the route claim itself (he never re-visits (24,7)) is proven per-tick by the automated test below, which this screenshot's tick (2025) falls inside the window of (wave 3: tick 2000-2055).

supportingAutomatedProof.why: A screenshot is one tick; the avoidance claim is about every tick of a route. This is the same claim, proven exhaustively rather than sampled, and it is what the interactive/screenshot commands above are pointing the owner's own eyes at.
supportingAutomatedProof.waveWindowForTheScreenshotTick: dotnet test tests/DungeonFortress.Simulation.Tests -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Report_the_returning_raiders_of_the_shipped_journals" reports, for baseline/seed 20260729: wave 3 raiderCount 7, endTick 2055 — the 2025 screenshot above is inside this wave's active window, which is why raiders including 'Крюк Немой' (returnedAsRaiderId 10) are on the map in it.
